definitions.explanation: The distance or route of a trip, or the journey itself. Used when discussing travel distance or the schedule of a trip.
A step or stage in a manufacturing or mechanical process, including the stroke of a piston or similar mechanism.

examples.japanese: {片道|かたみち}の{行程|こうてい}は{約|やく}3{時間|じかん}だ。
examples.english: The one-way journey is about three hours.

examples.japanese: {旅|たび}の{行程|こうてい}を{確認|かくにん}する。
{山頂|さんちょう}までの{行程|こうてい}は{険|けわ}しいが、{景色|けしき}は{素晴|すば}らしい。
examples.english: The journey to the summit is steep, but the scenery is wonderful.

examples.japanese: エンジンの{行程|こうてい}を{測定|そくてい}する。
この{機械|きかい}は4{行程|こうてい}サイクルで{動|うご}く。
examples.english: This machine operates on a four-stroke cycle.

examples.japanese: {製造|せいぞう}{行程|こうてい}の{各段階|かくだんかい}で{品質|ひんしつ}{検査|けんさ}を{行|おこな}う。
examples.english: Quality inspections are conducted at each stage of the manufacturing process.

notes: Composed of {行|こう} (go, travel) + {程|てい} (degree, extent, distance). Not to be confused with the homophone {工程|こうてい} (work process, production schedule), which focuses specifically on work/production steps, while {行程|こうてい} in sense 2 refers to mechanical strokes or stages. Common collocations: {行程|こうてい}{表|ひょう} (itinerary chart), {往復|おうふく}{行程|こうてい} (round-trip distance), {一日|いちにち}の{行程|こうてい} (a day's journey). In mountaineering and hiking, {行程|こうてい} specifically refers to the route distance and time estimate for the climb.
